Word Stress: the energy lexicon

Parts 1 and 2 together. Year 3, one session: the energy lexicon.

The rule

French rhythm is a machine gun. Every syllable the same length, the same force, rat-a-tat-a-tat. English rhythm is Morse code. Strong and weak alternate, and one syllable in each word stands out from the rest.

Amé-ri-que  →  three even syllables
A-ME-ri-ca  →  four syllables, one of them said, three thrown away

What "stressed" actually means: the stressed syllable is higher, stronger, longer. Not louder on its own. Higher in pitch, stronger in force, longer in time, all three at once.

And the other three? They go to the schwa: where the stress is not, the vowel goes to nothing. America is /əˈmerɪkə/, and two of its four vowels are the sound named after nothing.

The mark in the dictionary. When you look a word up you will see /ˈ/ before a syllable. That is the stress, and it goes in front of the syllable you lean on: nuclear is /ˈnjuːkliə/, so the stress is on nu. On this page we use CAPITALS instead, because they are easier to see: nuclear.

1 · Listening exercise

Before you learn any rule, learn to hear the shape of a word. ● is a strong syllable, • is a weak one. Say the word out loud, then pick its rhythm.

2 · The stress is not in the word. It is in the ending.

Find the ending. Count back. Done.
You do not need to know the word. You need to know the ending.
-ic(s)
-ical
-ity
-ive		 Stress the syllable just before it.
electric · atomic · economic · geopolitical · electricity · capacity · security · volatility · sustainability · intensive
-ion
-ial
-ious
-uate		 Stress the syllable just before it.
consumption · emissions · generation · electrification · transmission · distribution · regulation · solution · artificial · essential · industrial

3 · The procedure

Four steps. It works on words you have never seen.

vo · la · ti · li · ty
1Find the ending. Here it is -ity.
2That ending is in the "just before" list.
3Count back one syllable from the ending: ti.
4Say it higher, stronger, longer, and throw the other four away.
volatility   ••●••

Try it on a word you may not know: decarbonisation. Ending -ion, count back one, and you get decarbonisation. You may never have said that word before, and you now know how to pronounce it.

4 · Say it

Lean on the capitals. Tap any word to hear it first.

Consumption, emissions, generation, electrification: same ending, same beat. 🔊 Listen
The nuclear reactor needs regulation. 🔊 Listen
Capacity, security, volatility: count back one, every time. 🔊 Listen
Amé-ri-que is a machine gun. America is Morse code. 🔊 Listen

electricity electric consumption emissions generation electrification capacity security volatility regulation reactor nuclear

Word Stress: part 2

The rule

Find the ending. Count back.

In part 1 we saw that: -ic(s) -ical -ity -ive and -ion -ial -ious -uate all mean stress the syllable just before the ending.

This rule covers most of the words you will meet. There are three others that cover the rest of it.

5 · Three endings that do not count back one

-cy
-gy
-phy		 Stress two syllables before it. The only one that makes you count twice.
energy · technology · efficiency · intermittency · agency · geography
-ee
-eer
-oon		 Stress the ending itself. A doubled vowel takes the accent.
engineer · career · guarantee · trainee
-ment
-ful
-ness
-able		 Change nothing. These are the polite ones: the stress stays wherever the root word had it.
invest → investment · agree → agreement · renew → renewable

Notice what -eer does to engineer. It is the word you will say about yourselves more than any other, and the beat is on the last syllable: engineer, not engineer.

6 · Listening exercise

Same game as part 1, harder words. ● is a strong syllable, • is a weak one. Say the word out loud, then pick its rhythm.

7 · When the stress is the meaning

If a two-syllable word is both a noun and a verb, the noun takes the first syllable and the verb takes the second. Same letters. Different word.

nounan object a record a permit the increase a project
verbto object to record to permit to increase to project
Demand set a record.  ·  We record the demand. 🔊 Listen
The plant needs a permit.  ·  The state will not permit it. 🔊 Listen
This is the same fact as electricity, seen from the other side. There the ending moved the beat. Here the beat moves on its own and the word changes what it is. Stress is not decoration. It carries meaning.

A two-syllable word that is only a noun still takes the first syllable: a turbine, a pipeline, a network.

8 · Two things you are allowed to ignore

① The second beat. Long words often have a weaker second beat somewhere. Dictionaries mark it. It is not very audible and not particularly useful to know where it is. So do not learn it. One strong syllable per word is the job.

② Every exception at once. English borrowed from everywhere, so there are many. Machine came straight from French and kept the French beat: machine.

9 · Say it

Lean on the capitals. Tap any word to hear it first.

Energy, technology and efficiency all count back two. 🔊 Listen
An engineer with a career in nuclear. 🔊 Listen
The plant needs a permit. The state will not permit it. 🔊 Listen
The agreement is wrong: it is agreement, because agree was already there. 🔊 Listen
